$schema_note: The operator's record of which job_types the work_queue actually carries. scripts/validation/check-handler-coverage.mjs FAILS the worker image roll when any job_type listed here has no registered handler in the image.
why_this_file_exists: Most work_queue traffic is enqueued by pg_cron jobs created live with cron.schedule_in_database; their command bodies are not tracked in this repository at all (see supabase/migrations/20260904030000_ps22_retire_guc_secret_channel_general.sql). The checker can therefore only discover two producers statically (one SQL INSERT in a migration, one TypeScript insert in the onboarding route). Everything else has to be recorded here, from the live queue, or the gate is near-vacuous.

refresh.seeded_from: repository documentation (the pg_cron/schedule statements in each handler's header and in app/lib/jobs/register-*-handlers.ts) — NOT yet from the live queue
refresh.command: psql -d postgres -Atc "SELECT job_type, count(*) FROM work_queue WHERE created_at > now()-interval '14 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC"
how: 1. Run the command above against the operational database.
2. Replace the job_types array below with one entry per row: {"job_type": <col 1>, "count": <col 2>, "source": "proof query"}.
3. Set last_refreshed_from_database to the date you ran it.
4. Run `npm run jobs:handler-coverage:check`. A new job_type with no handler fails the gate here, in a PR, instead of dead-lettering rows after an image roll.

5. To compare the other direction, diff the handlers.txt the checker writes against `psql -d postgres -Atc "SELECT DISTINCT job_type FROM work_queue WHERE created_at > now()-interval '14 days' ORDER BY 1"`.
